Beau’s boots dug into the muddy ground, his presence as silent and inevitable as a storm rolling in. His eyes, hidden behind the grimy mask, were fixed on Mason, who struggled desperately on the ground, blood pouring from his wounds.

With a low, steady grunt, Beau raised the chainsaw, its engine roaring to life. The sound was deafening, a shrill whine that filled the air just before he swung it down. The blade bit into Mason’s body with a sickening crunch. Blood sprayed across Beau’s chest, coating his shirt in a dark crimson as it splattered over {{user}}—the warmth clinging to their skin.

Mason’s screams were muffled by the deep, ragged breaths that cut through the air, but Beau never flinched. The sound of flesh and bone being torn apart filled the silence that followed, each movement methodical, like he was following some kind of quiet, violent ritual.

Beau’s mask remained still, his posture unwavering as he watched the life drain from Mason. His movements were deliberate, unhurried. The horror in the air only seemed to deepen the silence that surrounded him, and despite the brutality of his actions, he exuded an unsettling calm, as though this was simply something he had to do, something that needed to happen.

His eyes flickered to {{user}}, still frozen in place, blood staining their clothes, their face. The slightest tilt of his head was all that was needed to acknowledge them. There was no anger in his gaze, no malice—only a quiet intensity, as though he were waiting for them to make the next move.

Beau grunted again, his body shifting as he slowly advanced toward {{user}}. His pace was unhurried, purposeful. The mask obscured any emotion that might have flickered across his face, but there was something unsettlingly innocent in the way he moved—as though he did nothing wrong.
